_policy: Size budget for the static export, enforced in CI by scripts/measure-export.mjs.
All values are uncompressed bytes on disk. GitHub Pages compresses text on the
wire, but the compressed size depends on its encoder, so the number a build can
reproduce is the number that gets gated.
These are ratchets, not fingerprints. A budget pinned to the exact current byte
count turns every honest pull request red, so each one carries headroom sized to
the change it should absorb before a human has to look, rounded up to the next
KiB. Regenerate with `npm run measure-export -- --update-budget`.
Every metric below is required and must be a positive whole number of bytes.
Missing or malformed values fail closed instead of silently disabling a gate.
totalBytes                +20%  everything, so content lands without a ceremony
javascriptBytes           +15%  moves with dependencies, not with content
cssBytes                  +15%  moves with the design system, not with content
fontBytes                 +15%  should only move when a family or axis changes
maxFileBytes              +20%  catches one unoptimised asset, the usual cause
maxRouteBootstrapBytes    +15%  document plus linked styles, scripts, preloads
distinctInlineSvgBytes    +20%  the icon set itself, each icon counted once
No gated metric may be a function of the page count. That is the rule the
list above is built to satisfy, because a gate a third blog post trips is a
gate people learn to ratchet without reading it.
The route bootstrap metric is intentionally not called first-load bytes: it
does not attribute images, media, srcset candidates, or CSS-referenced assets
to a route. Those files are still measured by subsystem and by totalBytes.
Missing same-origin bootstrap assets fail instead of making a route look smaller.
Inline SVG is gated on the distinct markup, which is the icon set itself: it
moves when an icon is added, swapped, or the library changes, and it does not
move when a page is added. The repeated total is printed instead, because it
is arithmetically the distinct markup times the page count. It is also only an
upper-bound deduplication opportunity rather than exact sprite savings, since
a sprite still needs definitions and per-use references.
HTML documents, RSC prefetch payloads, images, and repeated inline SVG bytes
are measured and printed but deliberately not gated: they grow with writing,
and a per-post failure trains people to raise the number without reading it. A
real regression in any of them still trips totalBytes.
